# Arithmetic scouting · Chapters 2–3 and 14 and Appendices A–B

Every code link fixes the inspected commit. “Port” identifies relevant source. Except for the locally checked items below, dependencies and transitive axioms still need verification against the project’s pin.

For B.6, the [prior formalizations follow-up](prior-formalizations.md) compares the OpenAI, Axiom and Hu half-planes and records the continuation and coefficient comparisons for reuse.

| Paper section and use | Formal precedent and remaining work |
|---|---|
| 2.1, test functions | The original report gives Anthropic’s locally compiled `NumberField.AdelicFourier.schwartzBruhat`. Hanke’s separate quadratic forms library proves adelic Poisson for an archimedean Schwartz function times local finite-place factors standard almost everywhere, including summability on both sides. The finite-place factor assumptions are explicit parameters. [QuadFormsKB.Analysis.adelicPoisson_factorizable](https://github.com/jonhanke/quadratic-forms-lean/blob/43bd01803a1f5ab5de0549a703544776b1cb978c/QuadFormsKB/Analysis/AdelicPoisson.lean) |
| 2.2, theta and Poisson | For summability and the zero-term convention start with the original report’s `NumberFieldKB.GlobalZeta.theta_eq_add`. For Thm 2.2.3.2 use the twisted Poisson theorem there. For norm-direction decay, `NumberFieldKB.GlobalZeta.isBigO_thetaInt_sub` concerns the integrated theta remainder. Estimates uniform in the idele class and its derivatives in 2.2.3.4 and 2.2.5.4 require further work. [theta estimates](https://github.com/jonhanke/algebraic-number-theory-lean/blob/5ea368e03a066197d53114efa8be66d351a9f060/NumberFieldKB/GlobalZeta/Decay.lean) |
| 2.3, S-local theta | `DedekindZetaZeroFree.PoissonS.ScaleShift.normalized_tensor_poisson` gives S-integer Poisson with archimedean Schwartz input and compactly supported locally constant finite-place factors. It assumes that S contains the different, with specified characters, measures and diagonal compatibility. Its additive S-integer summation and Masullo’s multiplicative S-unit averages need separate comparison. [SIntegerTensorCosets](https://github.com/AxiomMath/DedekindZetaZeroFree/blob/09afbb4ce6570c1615d58509dc197fc9f0956b7d/DedekindZetaZeroFree/HarmonicAnalysis/Poisson/SIntegerTensorCosets.lean) |
| 2.4 and A.4, S-unit counting, pp. 106–116 and 562–565 | Combine `NumberFieldKB.WeilBNT.finrank_gammaLattice` with `TauCeti.exists_abs_ncard_smul_inter_vadd_sub_le`, which estimates lattice counts in all translates uniformly by volume/covolume plus a boundary-order error. Prove the logarithmic box reduces to a dilated simplex in the sum-zero hyperplane, verify Lipschitz boundary and account for torsion, Haar normalization and rank zero. This supplies a route independent of re-formalizing Davenport’s proof. [S-unit lattice](https://github.com/jonhanke/algebraic-number-theory-lean/blob/5ea368e03a066197d53114efa8be66d351a9f060/NumberFieldKB/WeilBNT/SUnits.lean) · [translated lattice count](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/8794ab329bb60340fa690a2902cf995f0571721b/TauCeti/NumberTheory/GeometryOfNumbers/LatticePointCount.lean) |
| 3.1, character families | `NumberFieldKB.HeckeCharacter.norm_apply_eq_rpow_shift` supplies the real abscissa of a Hecke character. Its uniqueness and the norm-power twists give the parameters for the vertical strips. Supply the complex charts and handle the S-local quotient. [Hecke characters](https://github.com/jonhanke/algebraic-number-theory-lean/blob/5ea368e03a066197d53114efa8be66d351a9f060/NumberFieldKB/HeckeCharacter/Basic.lean) |
| 3.2, idelic Mellin transform | `NumberFieldKB.GlobalZeta.globalZeta_eq_mellin` unfolds the integral into the Mellin transform of the theta integral minus the constant term on Re(s)>1 for normalized characters and admissible functions. Use the theorem before transporting to Masullo’s normalizations or proving continuity in the strong-dual topology. [Mellin equality](https://github.com/jonhanke/algebraic-number-theory-lean/blob/5ea368e03a066197d53114efa8be66d351a9f060/NumberFieldKB/GlobalZeta/Decay.lean) |
| 3.3, local factors | `NumberFieldKB.LocalZeta.zetaIntegral_fourierV_eq_gammaFactorV` handles the nonarchimedean functional equation on the strip of absolute convergence. The real and complex Gaussian calculations are in `NumberFieldKB.LocalZeta.zetaIntegral_gaussian_real` and `NumberFieldKB.LocalZeta.zetaIntegral_gaussian_complex`. Take the finite product after matching Fourier measures. Poles, residues and estimates for general S-local inputs remain. [nonarchimedean](https://github.com/jonhanke/algebraic-number-theory-lean/blob/5ea368e03a066197d53114efa8be66d351a9f060/NumberFieldKB/LocalZeta/NonArchimedean.lean) · [real](https://github.com/jonhanke/algebraic-number-theory-lean/blob/5ea368e03a066197d53114efa8be66d351a9f060/NumberFieldKB/LocalZeta/Real.lean) · [complex](https://github.com/jonhanke/algebraic-number-theory-lean/blob/5ea368e03a066197d53114efa8be66d351a9f060/NumberFieldKB/LocalZeta/Complex.lean) |
| 3.4, Weil identities | `NumberFieldKB.GlobalZeta.globalZeta_eq_archZeta_mul_tprod` factorizes a global integral where it converges. It supplies the initial product for 3.4.1.1. Check the normalized continuation to Re(s)>0. I found no exact formalization of the one-dimensional eigendistribution assertion 3.4.3.3. [factorization](https://github.com/jonhanke/algebraic-number-theory-lean/blob/5ea368e03a066197d53114efa8be66d351a9f060/NumberFieldKB/GlobalZeta/EulerProduct.lean) |
| A.1, norm-one classes | `NumberFieldKB.Ideles.IdeleClassGroup.isCompact_normOne` proves compactness for the norm-one subgroup of the global idele class group. Distinguish S-local groups from full ideles that are units outside S. [norm-one compactness](https://github.com/jonhanke/algebraic-number-theory-lean/blob/5ea368e03a066197d53114efa8be66d351a9f060/NumberFieldKB/Ideles/Compact.lean) |
| A.2–A.3, fundamental domain and measures | `DedekindZetaZeroFree.KPAdditiveFundamentalDomain.isAddFundamentalDomain` and `domain_mass` handle the archimedean parallelepiped times the finite integral adeles. `QuadFormsKB.Tamagawa.Measure.Weil.fundamentalDomain_mul_eq_one` gives a complementary covolume identity. Match the paper’s additive and multiplicative local factors before transport. [adelic fundamental domain](https://github.com/AxiomMath/DedekindZetaZeroFree/blob/09afbb4ce6570c1615d58509dc197fc9f0956b7d/DedekindZetaZeroFree/Adeles/Lattices/AdditiveFundamentalDomain.lean) · [adelic lattice](https://github.com/jonhanke/quadratic-forms-lean/blob/43bd01803a1f5ab5de0549a703544776b1cb978c/QuadFormsKB/Tamagawa/Measure/Weil/AdelicLattice.lean) |
| A.5, Hardy–Littlewood and differentiation | `Measurable.measurableEmbedding` supplies the standard Borel injective-map theorem A.5.2.8. `hasWeakType_maximalFunction_one` supplies a ball maximal inequality in separable doubling metric measure spaces. `VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_average` supplies differentiation. Prove the covering hypotheses for the actual idelic neighborhoods before applying either result on a general locally compact abelian group. [Borel embedding](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/fc4f59e577feb1a4956671bc04ac18aaaf8cd842/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Constructions/Polish/Basic.lean) · [Carleson](https://github.com/fpvandoorn/carleson/blob/f7487cc9da4d1e73f009dc0280cd5b958f3e2c78/Carleson/ToMathlib/HardyLittlewood.lean) · [Vitali differentiation](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/fc4f59e577feb1a4956671bc04ac18aaaf8cd842/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Covering/Differentiation.lean) |
| B.1, convexity | `PhragmenLindelof.vertical_strip` is the interpolation tool. `DedekindZetaZeroFree.detector_convexity_bridge` has a conductor/height bound for primitive ray characters over totally complex fields with explicit strip and conductor restrictions. The unrestricted infinite-order Hecke case requires the appropriate boundary bounds and gamma asymptotics. [Mathlib](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/fc4f59e577feb1a4956671bc04ac18aaaf8cd842/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/PhragmenLindelof.lean) · [weak convexity](https://github.com/AxiomMath/DedekindZetaZeroFree/blob/09afbb4ce6570c1615d58509dc197fc9f0956b7d/DedekindZetaZeroFree/LFunctions/Hecke/UniformWeakConvexity.lean) |
| B.2–B.3, Mellin inversion and contours | `mellinInv_mellin_eq` proves scalar or Banach-valued inversion assuming vertical integrability. `Complex.integral_boundary_rect_eq_zero_of_differentiableOn` handles finite rectangles. For unbounded contours, AINTLIB’s explicit formula implements height selection and boundary estimates for particular completed L-functions. Prove the horizontal integrals vanish under the paper’s hypotheses. [inversion](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/fc4f59e577feb1a4956671bc04ac18aaaf8cd842/Mathlib/Analysis/MellinInversion.lean) · [Cauchy rectangles](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/fc4f59e577feb1a4956671bc04ac18aaaf8cd842/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/CauchyIntegral.lean) · [contour application](https://github.com/CBirkbeck/AINTLIB/blob/c3bc9bfafaf32cf281da174a7ec287c1e56acc99/projects/DedekindResidue/DedekindResidue/ExplicitFormula/WeilAssembly.lean) |
| B.4, explicit formula | `DedekindResidue.weil_explicit_formula` assembles the Weil–Poitou identity for Dedekind zeta over **any number field**, with conditions on an even test function, boundary estimates and variation. `DedekindResidue.weil_explicit_formula_auxF` discharges them for a specified family. Reuse the divisor/contour, prime and gamma parts for the trivial character. The general character and idelic principal-value test-function versions B.4.2.2 and B.4.4.7 require further identification. [WeilAssembly](https://github.com/CBirkbeck/AINTLIB/blob/c3bc9bfafaf32cf281da174a7ec287c1e56acc99/projects/DedekindResidue/DedekindResidue/ExplicitFormula/WeilAssembly.lean) |
| B.5, Kronecker–Weyl | `D5.S3.Fourier.Asymptotics.TorusOrbitEquidistribution.result` gives convergence of discrete orbit averages to Haar on the closure of powers for any finite torus element and any continuous observable. **Compiled unmodified on this project’s pin and passed the three-axiom check.** B.5.2.1 uses a continuous-time orbit, Riemann-integrable inputs and the rank of its closure. The Fourier-character/approximation proof supplies a template. [torus result](https://github.com/the-omega-institute/trureturing/blob/5ab3bcb5f8ecc87840489720502d828a4f549cd6/D5/S3/Fourier/Asymptotics/TorusOrbitEquidistribution.lean) |
| B.6, zero-free region | `HeckeSevenEighths.heckeL_zeroFree` gives a continuation of the ideal series, nonzero off its possible simple pole for Re(s)>7/8, for all number fields and Circle-valued idele-class characters, including infinite order. Match the ideal coefficients to `NumberField.HeckeCharacter.LSeries` using `NumberField.HeckeCharacter.IsUnramifiedAt.localValue_eq`. This fixed strip can supply a zero-free neighborhood in B.6.1.1. Logarithmic derivative and reciprocal growth estimates still need proofs. Also `DedekindZetaZeroFree.heckeCorollary` covers finite ray characters on Re(s)>31/32. [unitary Hecke endpoint](https://github.com/Rogerhu12/hecke-seven-eighths/blob/c77efa9237c4635ed61933fbca98722c359c984a/src/Solution/HeckeSevenEighthsSolution.lean) · [Mathlib local value](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/fc4f59e577feb1a4956671bc04ac18aaaf8cd842/Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/HeckeLFunction.lean) · [Dedekind and ray-class endpoints](https://github.com/AxiomMath/DedekindZetaZeroFree/blob/09afbb4ce6570c1615d58509dc197fc9f0956b7d/Solution/DedekindZetaSolution.lean) |
| B.7, boundary Euler products | `NumberFieldKB.NonVanishing.heckeLCont_ne_zero_of_one_le_re` proves nonvanishing for unitary characters excluding norm powers. `NumberFieldKB.NonVanishing.hasProd_localL_one_normOrder` proves norm-ordered convergence of the Euler product **at s=1 for nontrivial finite-order characters**. B.7 also needs arbitrary characters, uniformity, derivatives or estimates as appropriate to its individual claims. [nonvanishing and boundary Euler product](https://github.com/jonhanke/algebraic-number-theory-lean/blob/5ea368e03a066197d53114efa8be66d351a9f060/NumberFieldKB/NonVanishing/Hecke.lean) |
| 14.1, multiplicity discussion | `BrauerInduction.exists_trace_eq_sum_zsmul_induced_linearCharacter` expresses the trace of a finite-group representation as an integral sum of induced linear characters. This can help with the group-theoretic input only. 14.1.2.3 states additional assumptions including global Langlands, GRH and GSH. [Brauer induction](https://github.com/anthropics/fermats-last-theorem/blob/6e837e75355538c7f80bab5b956861e86c4eacc2/Theorems/Thm_BrauerInduction_exists_trace_eq_sum_zsmul_induced_linearCharacter.lean) |
| 14.2–14.3, function fields and higher rank | `NumberFieldKB.WeilBNT.FF.weil_VII_6_thm4_ff` gives the function-field zeta numerator of degree twice the genus under the constant-field hypothesis. It can support 14.2’s comparison. Its polynomial identity alone supplies no eigenvalue absolute-value bound. On p. 536, 14.3 introduces a proposed GL(n) extension and ends with an editorial footnote. [function-field zeta](https://github.com/jonhanke/algebraic-number-theory-lean/blob/5ea368e03a066197d53114efa8be66d351a9f060/NumberFieldKB/WeilBNT/FunctionField/ZetaFinal.lean) |

**Checks.** Sources above use Apache-2.0. Hanke’s two projects and trureturing use Lean 4.35.0, Anthropic uses 4.33.1, AINTLIB uses 4.36.0-rc2, Carleson uses 4.36.0-rc1, TauCeti uses 4.37.0-rc1, and AxiomMath/DedekindZetaZeroFree and Rogerhu12/hecke-seven-eighths use 4.35.0-rc3. The pinned Mathlib names were elaborated in `.agent/ScoutArithmeticCheck.lean`, with three-axiom checks for inversion, strip bounds and Vitali differentiation. The discrete torus lemma has the same local axiom check. The cited external theorem bodies contain no direct `sorry` at the inspected locations. Rogerhu12’s upstream comparator passed for the exact solution tree: commit 43102897 has the same Git tree (90226143) as c77efa92. Its allowlist has only the three permitted axioms. AxiomMath reports an upstream build. Neither library was ported or rebuilt here.
